start.text: Welcome to station three! This is the Stratasys uPrint SE / SE Plus, an FDM 3D printer.

main2.text: This printer uses ABSplus thermoplastic to create durable parts. It's useful for prototypes and functional engineering models.

choices.label: What do you mean by functional?

main3.text: The printer can also build soluble support material around the part. That helps make more complicated shapes possible.

main4.text: After printing, those supports have to be removed. That's where post-processing becomes part of the workflow.

main5.text: So this printer can create durable parts with complex geometry. It's another way engineers turn CAD designs into physical parts.

choices.label: How is this different from the others?

main6.text: That's station three! Next, find number four to see what happens after certain parts finish printing.

fdm.text: FDM stands for Fused Deposition Modeling. The printer deposits heated thermoplastic one layer at a time.

choices.label: So it builds from the bottom up?

fdm_layers.text: Exactly! Each thin layer is placed on the one below it. Together, those layers build the complete 3D part.

absplus.text: ABSplus is the thermoplastic this system uses for the model. It's made for durable prototypes and engineering parts.

durability.text: Sometimes engineers want to test more than appearance. A stronger prototype can help test fit, handling, or function.

functional.text: A functional prototype helps test how a design actually behaves. It's more than just checking what the part looks like.

choices.label: Can you give me an example?

functional_example.text: For example, you might print a bracket or fixture to check its size and fit before making the final version.

soluble_support.text: The support is temporary material printed with the model. Compatible support material can later be dissolved away.

choices.label: Why not just pull it off?

why_support.text: Some designs have overhangs or sections with nothing underneath them. Supports hold those areas while they're being printed.

why_soluble.text: Soluble support is useful for complex or hard-to-reach geometry. It can be removed without manually pulling every support away.

support_removal.text: The support can be dissolved using a compatible cleaning process. We actually have equipment here that does that.

comparison.text: Each printer has different strengths and workflows. This system focuses on FDM parts using ABSplus and soluble supports.

station4_tease.text: Station four is the support-cleaning system. It shows what happens to certain printed parts after they leave the printer.

bye.text: Sounds good! When you're ready, look for number four to finish the 3D printing workflow.
